notes.1: This question was generally well done with many candidates scoring both marks. Several different approaches were possible, all of which were seen. Answer: Angle of projection is 41.8°
notes.2i: This part of the question involved taking moments about the point A. Some candidates resolved the 10 N force horizontally and vertically before taking moments and then omitted to use one of them. The correct equation should be 10cos30x1.2sinθ-10sin30x1.2cosθ=6x0.8sinθ. The candidates who firstly found the perpendicular distance from A to the 10 N force more often than not went on to find θ correctly. The correct equation this time was 10x1.2sin(θ - 30) = 6x0.8sinθ.
notes.2iii: This part of the question required the candidates to find the friction force F and the normal reaction R. They then needed to use F = µR, where µ is the coefficient of friction. Answers: (i) θ = 47.0° (ii) µ = 0.532
notes.3i: This part of the question was generally well done.
notes.3iii: Here a 3 term energy equation is required. Often the EE term was omitted and only a PE term and a KE term appeared. Answers: (i) Extension = 0.2 m (ii) Speed of projection of P = 2.83 ms–1 (iii) Speed of P when the string first becomes slack = 2.45 ms–1 �PAGE�40
notes.4i: There were many correct methods possible for this part of the question. The quickest and neatest method was to use the energy equation mx202 - mx182 = mgh. Some candidates simply said 182 = 202 - 2gh which is not acceptable.
notes.4iii: Again here there were many correct methods possible. This part of the question proved to be very difficult for many candidates. A good neat solution was to use s = 3.8 from part (i) and substitute into s = ut + at2/2. This gave 3.8 = (20sin40)T - gT2/2, T = 2.230 and 0.341. Hence time required = 2.230 - 0.341 = 1.89s. Horizontal distance = (20cos40)x1.89=29.0m. Answers: (i) Height of P above the ground = 3.8m. (ii) Time speed of P is less than 18ms–1=1.8 s and horizontal distance=29.0m.
notes.5: This question proved to be the most difficult question on the paper.
notes.5i: Some candidates used the incorrect formula for the centre of mass of the semi-circular arc. Too many candidates used 1.8m as the diameter and not the radius. Often the value found for the centre of mass of the semi-circular arc was left as the final answer.
notes.5iii: Here again a wrong formula was often used for the centre of mass of the semi-circular lamina. Not many candidates managed to set up a correct moment equation and, of those who did, the accuracy was often not very good. Too many terms were prematurely approximated. Answers: (i) Distance of centre of mass of frame from O = 0.700m. (ii) Weight of frame = 37.3 N.

notes.general_comments:
Most candidates produced work that was neat, well presented and clearly argued but there were a few
exceptions to this.
Only a few candidates used g = 9.8 or 9.81 instead of the value of 10 recommended in the rubric.
Candidates should be reminded to refer to the formula booklet for certain formulae which they may need in
answering questions.
Candidates found questions 1, 6 and 7 to be easiest and questions 3(ii), (iii), 4(ii) and 5 to be hardest.
